card.summary: The S. 3265 bill amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to extend, modify, and enhance the Work Opportunity Tax Credit through December 31, 2030. It adjusts credit percentages for first-year wages, adds inflation adjustments, alters rules for specific categories such as veterans and summer youth, removes certain age limits for food assistance recipients, expands eligibility to include qualified military spouses, and directs federal agencies to promote hiring targeted workers in critical industries.

summary: H.R. 6231, titled the 'Improve and Enhance the Work Opportunity Tax Credit Act,' amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. The bill extends the Work Opportunity Tax Credit through December 31, 2030, updates credit calculations and wage limits, introduces cost-of-living adjustments, removes an age limit for certain food assistance recipients, expands eligibility to military spouses, and directs federal agencies to promote targeted hiring within critical industries.

affected_groups.effect: May qualify for updated and extended tax credits when hiring individuals from targeted groups who begin work after December 31, 2025.
Subject to updated wage limitations, percentages, and calculation rules regarding the tax credit.
affected_groups.group: Certain Veterans, Summer Youth Employees, and Long-Term Family Assistance Recipients

affected_groups.effect: Individuals over age 40 become eligible for the credit as the age limit is removed.
Spouses of members of the Armed Forces are added as a newly eligible targeted group for the hiring credit.

key_provisions: Extends the expiration date of the Work Opportunity Tax Credit from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2030.
Modifies credit calculations for first-year wages, providing a 50 percent rate for certain wage thresholds and longer-service employment.
Adds an annual cost-of-living adjustment starting after 2025 for specific wage limits tied to the tax credit.
Removes the upper age limit restriction for qualified Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits recipients.
Expands tax credit eligibility to include qualified military spouses who are spouses of members of the Armed Forces.
Directs specific federal department secretaries and the Small Business Administration administrator to promote the hiring of targeted group members to business leaders in critical industries.
